# Writing a `concept` page

Generated from `concept`'s own template declarations. It states what this type requires;
the rules that apply to every page are in `wiki-authoring-spec.md` beside this file.

- **Lives at** `<domain>/concepts/<kebab-name>.md` — pick the sub-wiki by what the concept must cite, not by who is interested in it: a term true regardless of our product is `domain/`, a speculative or cross-cutting product idea is `product/`, an interaction or accessibility standard is `design/`, an operational model is `operations/`, and governance vocabulary is `governance/`. Shallowest home whose layer covers its citations wins. A cross-cutting product policy — a rule the product enforces everywhere rather than one feature's own idea — lives instead at `product/concepts/policies/<kebab-name>.md`
- **Authorship** `curated` — an agent may draft it; a human approves
- **Freshness** stale after 365d
- **Template version** 1 — set `template-version: 1`

## Frontmatter

The type table demands no field beyond the base set.

The template also scaffolds `template-version`, `sources`, `related`, `confidence` — fill or empty each one; leaving a placeholder is an error.

## Placeholders to replace

{{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{OWNER}} {{CONFIDENCE}}. Leaving one in place is an error (`unsubstituted-token`), and so is leaving a template example line (`template-example-line`).

## Where this type may link

**Written in `domain/`** (layer 0):

You may link to other pages in `domain/` and to no other sub-wiki: nothing sits below it.

You may not link to `product/`, `design/`, `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

**Written in `product/`** (layer 1):

You may link to `domain/` — and to other pages in `product/`.

You may not link to `design/`, `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

**Written in `design/`** (layer 2):

You may link to `domain/`, `product/` — and to other pages in `design/`.

You may not link to `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

**Written in `operations/`** (layer 4):

You may link to `domain/`, `product/`, `design/`, `engineering/` — and to other pages in `operations/`.

You may not link to `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

**Written in `governance/`** (layer 6):

You may link to `domain/`, `product/`, `design/`, `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/` — and to other pages in `governance/`.

## Sections

Keep every heading, in this order: `## Definition`, `## Usage`, `## Examples`, `## Non-examples`, `## Boundaries`, `## Related concepts`.

**These may not be answered `None.`** — they must carry content: `## Definition`.

## What the audit checks on this page

Because of the declarations above: template-sections, section-order, required-section-content. Every page is also checked for empty sections, heading restatement, callout types and code pointers. Run `/wiki-conformance-audit` to see the full list with its verdict.

## After you save

Two steps finish the page and neither is in the template:

- Commit the file under your own identity — authorship is a git fact, not a frontmatter one.
- Run `/wiki-reindex` so the page appears in its sub-wiki `index.md` and in `_derived/cited-by.md`. Until then it exists but nothing links to it.
